items.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024
items.q: Maria Schneider said much the same.

ctx.x: I don’t have that skill. And I was, quite frankly, too enamored with the drums themselves to even take the time to learn the technology. Because I had things I needed to work on just from my own musical standpoint. And so yeah, the changes in the past 40, 50 years have been remarkable. And in a lot of ways I think the way I learned, primarily through mentorship, I hope isn’t lost with what’s coming down the pike with all the artificial intelligence technologies. And it’s — I’m sure there will always be mentors, I…
Maria Schneider said much the same. She said you have to live life in order to put it into your music.

Yeah, exactly. So yeah, self-realization is, well you can help a student with that. And what I found as a teacher is that the more you can relate to your own development, the problems that you had when you were their age or younger. I mean that helped me remarkably is to think about now what I would have done if I were his age and confronted with this. And drawing on my own experience, that’s why those days of playing with Jimmy Ford and Arnett was so valuable is because it gave me so much, I mean oh God, it’s…
